short: Counting common bases of two matroids

title.title: Approximate counting of common matroid bases
title.subtitle: Claim: a polynomial-time randomized scheme counts the common bases of two matroids given by oracles

plain: Count the choices that obey two separate rulebooks at once, quickly and almost exactly

beats.text: Schematically: each matroid has its family of bases; count the ones they share
Bipartite perfect matchings are the common bases of two partition matroids
Claimed: approximate that count in polynomial time, with independence oracles

steps: Recast shared choices as picking one from each pair
Give imperfect picks a weight; start where totals are known
Slowly lower that weight, random-walking at each stage
A key inequality shows each walk settles fast

achievement.label: Counting common bases of two matroids (open)
achievement.context: Before: one matroid (Anari–Liu–Oveis Gharan–Vinzant, 2019) and bipartite matchings (Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda)
achievement.note: Oracle model; the polynomial degrees are unspecified

verify.detail: In Lean: the two-matroid FPRAS. The polymatroid extension is not formalized
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: Counting choices that obey two rulebooks.
Many objects are choices allowed by two rulebooks at once, like matchings and spanning trees.
Imperfect picks are weighted, then the weight is lowered, sampling at each stage.

sources.quote: Anari-Liu-Oveis Gharan-Vinzant (STOC 2019) all matroids via log-concave polynomials
Counting common bases of two matroids generalizes bipartite perfect matchings (JSV) and was a well-known open problem.
partial formalization: CommonBasesFPRAS.lean covers the two-matroid result; the polymatroid paper is not formalized
